lead.headline: Down 79.62 Sunday. Won by 1.58 Monday.
lead.dek: AB81 needed 40.75 from two players on the last night of the week. It got 42.32, and now it sits alone in first place at 7-1.
body: I’ve covered this team for eight weeks and I have stopped trying to explain it. At 2:13 p.m. Sunday, AB81 trailed Maye I touch your TDs? by 79.62. That isn’t a deficit. That’s a zip code. A little more than a day later AB81 was 7-1, alone in first place, winner by 1.58.

The hole was real. Christian Watson banked a pile for the champ on Thursday night, Drake Maye finished with 22.46, Harold Fannin Jr. scored 23.4 and Bucky Irving added 21.0. The champ closed its books at 122.72 on Sunday and had nobody left to play. AB81 entered Monday with 81.98 and two men standing: Sam Darnold and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The number was 40.75. Every other member of this roster had already gone home.

Smith-Njigba made it a game right before the half. At 6:35 p.m. Pacific, Darnold hit him for a 43-yard touchdown, a 17.02-point swing on one snap, and the gap went from 29.96 to 12.94. For the next two hours the champ, finished and helpless, got to watch the number shrink. Darnold’s fourth-quarter touchdown and two-point conversion cut deeper. So did a last possession that finally pushed AB81 over the line. Final tally for the duo: Darnold 18.52, Smith-Njigba 23.8. That’s 42.32, or 1.57 more than the math demanded.

Now the arithmetic the champ has to live with. Jaylen Waddle scored 14.9 on its bench while Drake London scored 1.8 in the lineup. Aaron Jones Sr. scored 6.0 on the bench while Zay Flowers scored 0.0 in the lineup. Either swap wins this game by itself. Best possible lineup: 141.82. Last week this team won by 0.86. This week the fantasy gods sent the invoice.

AB81’s own save came from a place nobody expected: the transaction log. A franchise that made zero moves for seven weeks made three in about three minutes on Sunday afternoon, and the two new starters produced 15.6 points. More on that in Smart Move.

Don’t mistake any of this for dominance. AB81 is sixth in the league with 1,233.02 points. Its all-play record is 28-28, which is the record of a .500 team. Luck is worth 3.0 wins, the most in R.A.T.S., and its last two wins came with 122.08 and 124.3 points, the kind of totals that lose most weeks. It’s 4-1 in games decided by fewer than 10 points over two seasons. I can’t tell you why. I can only tell you the standings, and the standings say first.

games.headline: Cherry Blossom hits 198.54, makes it four straight
games.dek: Seven lead changes in 50 minutes on Sunday morning, then none. deeboliciouskins has now lost three in a row.
games.pull: Seven lead changes before lunch. Zero after.
body: For 50 minutes on Sunday this was the best game in the league. The lead changed hands seven times between 10:16 and 11:06 a.m. Ja’Marr Chase kept yanking it back for deeboliciouskins, including on a 30-yard touchdown at 10:49. Brock Bowers ended the argument with a 5-yard catch at 11:06 that put Cherry Blossom up 47.46 to 46.04. It never trailed again.

Then Tee Higgins went to work. He finished with 37.5, the biggest game by any starter in this matchup, and he had help everywhere: Bowers 28.2, Puka Nacua 25.0, Jaylen Warren 21.3 and Jonah Coleman, a 9:36 p.m. Saturday pickup, 20.4. By 4:29 p.m. Sunday the lead was 75.74.

deeboliciouskins did not go quietly. D’Andre Swift scored 27.9 on Monday night and Chase finished with 31.1, but Patrick Mahomes scored 25.44 on the bench while Jayden Daniels scored 14.98 at quarterback. Final: 198.54 to 166.68. Even a perfect lineup would have stopped at 195.24.

games.headline: A perfect lineup flattens Poochinski
games.dek: Bad things man bad things left 0.0 points on its bench, led from Thursday’s opening drive and banked 181.84.
body: Bad things man bad things took the lead on Thursday’s opening drive and never gave it back. It was 83.14 up at 1:38 p.m. Sunday. Kirk Cousins scored 28.18 at quarterback, Michael Wilson 26.8, Chuba Hubbard 24.9, Matthew Golden 20.9, Trey McBride 20.2. It was the only perfect lineup anyone set all week.
Last week this team blew a 39.34-point lead and lost a game its bench could have won. This week the best thing on the bench was 6.9 points from Ollie Gordon II, and nobody cared. Lesson received.

Poochinski’s weekend was a slow leak: Chris Godwin Jr. was added at 6:19 a.m. Sunday, started and scored 0.0. CeeDee Lamb had 12.8, Dak Prescott 19.8. Monday’s trio made the score respectable and did something more useful besides. Final: 181.84 to 134.28.

games.headline: Six straight losses end with a 107-point lead
games.dek: Big Stric Energy scored 181.48 in the league’s saddest game of the year. Joe Burrow’s 42.48 was not enough to make it close.
body: Billed as the game neither team deserved to win. Big Stric Energy made sure somebody did. Jordan Love hit Tucker Kraft from 12 yards at 5:37 p.m. Thursday, hit Josh Jacobs at 7:14 p.m. and the stack finished with 63.02. Santa Clara’s Finest didn’t score a point on Thursday. By 1:08 p.m. Sunday the lead was 107.38.

Josh Allen scored 27.56. Braelon Allen scored 23.3, including a 21-yard touchdown. The Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST, a Wednesday pickup, scored 20.0. Everything worked, which on this beat counts as breaking news.
Santa Clara’s Finest got 42.48 from Burrow and 29.9 from Bhayshul Tuten and still lost by 45.0, because Lamar Jackson scored 0.0 in the other quarterback slot. Final: 181.48 to 136.48.

beats.headline: Three moves in three minutes, and first place
body: For seven weeks the running joke on this beat was the blank transaction log. Then at 3:06 p.m. Sunday, this front office added Makai Lemon. At 3:09 it added Darius Cooper. Both started. The moves were the difference in a game decided by 1.58.
7-1. Alone in first. The lead over the league’s next two teams is one full game, and both of them have outscored AB81 by about 100 points.
I said last week the evidence was don’t touch anything. The evidence has been updated. Touch something, on a Sunday, at the last possible moment.
beats.insight: Enjoy first place, then fix the receivers. Carnell Tate is on bye, and the projected lineup has Makai Lemon in a WR slot at 5.02. Ladd McConkey is on waivers at a 12.0 projection. George Kittle returns at 14.94, but Cherry Blossom is still a 69.1% favorite. Luck is worth 3.0 wins so far, the most in the league, and it won’t stay that high.

beats.headline: Lost by 47.56, won the tiebreak by 0.68
body: A 47.56-point loss is a strange week to gain ground, but here we are. Poochinski entered Monday needing 34.91 from Caleb Williams, Luther Burden III and the Seattle Seahawks D/ST to move past Bad things man bad things on points. They scored 35.58.

That’s why the standings say second, not third: 1,332.72 points to 1,332.04, the tiniest of edges at 6-2. Burden’s 1-yard touchdown at 5:30 p.m. Monday was worth 11.14 by itself, and the 18.6 he finished with is what kept a blowout from costing a spot in the standings.

The bad news: the last three weeks average 147.93, down from a season average of 166.59. The waiver-wire addition of Chris Godwin Jr. at 6:19 a.m. Sunday went straight into the lineup and scored 0.0. This front office has five moves all year. That one won’t make the highlight reel.
beats.insight: Chris Olave returns at a 18.07 projection, and this lineup leads the league at 184.24. Javonte Williams still gets 39% of his points from touchdowns, so don’t read his 6.7 as a crisis or his big weeks as a promise. A 69.3% favorite against the champ, with a 75.5% shot at a top-two seed. Just don’t start anybody who was added at dawn.

beats.headline: Twenty-four moves, and this time every one worked
body: At 6:25 p.m. Thursday, with Week 8 already under way, this front office added Kirk Cousins. He scored 28.18, the best pickup in the league. Cincinnati’s defense and Evan McPherson, both Wednesday waiver claims, scored 7.0 and 5.0 for good measure.
Twenty-four moves in 2026, the most in the league, and a week after the bench cost this team a game, it left exactly 0.0 points on the pine.
Now the bad news. It finished Monday night on the couch, third in the standings by 0.68 points.
beats.insight: A deep quarterback room (four available) is a luxury in a 2-QB league, and it’s also this team’s trade chip if anyone ever trades. Ollie Gordon II is the usage story: 24.0 opportunities a game over two weeks on an 82% snap share, projected 13.68. A 60.4% favorite over Big Stric Energy, and a 59% shot at a top-two seed.

beats.headline: Four straight, 198.54, and suddenly nobody wants this team
body: Four weeks ago this team had not won a game. Now it’s 4-4 on a four-game winning streak, averaging 179.16 over the last three weeks. That’s the best in the league by a distance.

Saturday night’s move was the sharp one: Jonah Coleman at 9:36 p.m., straight into the lineup, 20.4 points. The dropped Cameron Dicker had 11.0 and Jake Bates scored 6.0, so it cost something at kicker. Nobody here is asking for a refund.
It still left Bo Nix’s 19.28 on the bench behind Jared Goff’s 10.04. The worst thing you can say about this lineup is that it could have scored 207.78.
beats.insight: Christian McCaffrey is back at a 22.2 projection, which more than covers Jaylen Warren’s bye. The real call is at quarterback: four are available, and Goff’s 10.04 is not the reason you own him. Bo Nix belongs in the conversation. A 69.1% favorite over AB81, and playoff odds of 99.5%. This is the team I’d want to avoid in December.

beats.headline: Three straight losses and one saved tiebreak
body: This franchise ranks third in the league in points and has lost three in a row. That sentence should come with a warning label. Week 8 had Ja’Marr Chase at 31.1, Tony Pollard at 28.7 and D’Andre Swift at 27.9, and it wasn’t close to enough.

The bench report is rough: 28.56 points left, including Patrick Mahomes’ 25.44 and DJ Moore’s 16.6. Even so, the best lineup here falls 3.3 short of Cherry Blossom’s number. Sometimes the other guy just has it.
Swift’s Monday did protect one thing. deeboliciouskins needed 23.87 from him and Jason Myers to stay ahead of Cherry Blossom on points. They scored 28.9, and it stays fourth.
beats.insight: Pollard is on bye, and he’s the team’s hottest back: 27.0 opportunities a game on a 78% snap share. Rachaad White (14.0 last week) is the obvious fill. Start Mahomes, who projects at 20.83 to Daniels’ 16.99. Swift gets 40% of his points from touchdowns, so don’t pay for last week. A 76.1% favorite against Santa Clara’s Finest. Losing streaks don’t get a better exit than that.

beats.headline: The champ’s lineup lost the game the champ was winning
body: Week 7, this franchise won by 0.86. Week 8, it lost by 1.58. Add those up and you have the season: nothing is free, and everything is close.

The Wednesday work was fine: Jacoby Brissett off waivers to cover Brock Purdy’s bye, Matt Gay in at kicker. Brissett scored 4.46, which is not fine. Fannin (23.4), Maye (22.46) and Irving (21.0) built a lead of 79.62, and that lead lasted until two players on the other side got a Monday night stage all to themselves.
Sixth place, a playoff spot and a 2-6 record. The cushion over Big Stric Energy is 53.02 points on the tiebreak, and that’s all that’s holding this thing up.
beats.insight: Purdy is back at 22.47, which fixes the quarterback math. Now fix the receivers: Waddle’s 14.9 on the bench was the game. Aaron Jones Sr. is a trap, though; his opportunities fell from 23.0 to 8.0 a game and his snap share from 73% to 33%. Playoff odds fell to 70.3%, and next up is Poochinski at 30.7% to win. This is the week to steal one.

beats.headline: Six straight losses are over. Math remains.
body: The streak is dead. 181.48 was plenty, and it came with the kind of front-office work that’s been missing: Chase McLaughlin (12.0) and the Jaguars D/ST (20.0), both added on Wednesday, both started, both useful.

I’d like to stop there. I can’t. Rashee Rice scored 18.3 on the bench while DK Metcalf scored 1.4. Dalton Kincaid scored 18.6 on the bench while Jalen Coker scored 9.6. Geno Smith scored 19.0 on the bench, because in this franchise the bench is always in form. 28.0 points left, in a win.
A 2-6 team with a 29.1% chance at the playoffs, up from 17.3% a week ago. You’ll take it.
beats.insight: Metcalf is on bye, which makes this one easy: Rashee Rice starts. Nico Collins is back at 16.21. Keep trusting Braelon Allen, whose opportunities rose from 14.5 to 23.5 a game on an 80% snap share. Ashton Jeanty is the worry, down from 22.3 to 11.0 opportunities. A 39.6% shot at Bad things man bad things, and 53.02 points behind the champ on the tiebreak, so both a win and a big score matter.

beats.headline: The quarterback room is now a quarterback
body: Here is a sentence I wrote last week: this front office drafted two first-round quarterbacks and has somehow ended up short on quarterbacks. Week 8 took that as a challenge.

At 5:46 p.m. Thursday it dropped Aaron Rodgers for Blake Corum. Lamar Jackson then scored 0.0 in a starting quarterback slot. Rodgers scored 5.88 for nobody. Burrow’s 42.48 and Tuten’s 29.9 were wasted, and the team fell to 1-7.
1,102.52 points, fewest in the league. Nineteen moves. Playoff odds 2%. The franchise run by PurdyAvg continues to not roster Brock Purdy, and at this point it could use him.
beats.insight: The projected lineup has an empty QB slot, and that is not a figure of speech. Malik Willis (17.48), J.J. McCarthy (16.65) and Baker Mayfield (15.43) are on waivers; claim one Wednesday. Colston Loveland (11.5) belongs in the lineup over Hunter Henry (6.0). Even with a fix, this team is 23.9% to beat deeboliciouskins.

rankings.blurb: Perfect lineup, 181.84, best pickup of the week. The best team in the league. Third by 0.68.
Most points in the league and a tiebreak saved on Monday night. The 47.56-point loss stings less than it should.
7-1, alone in first, sixth in points, 28-28 in the all-play. We have stopped asking.
Four straight wins and a 198.54. The hottest team in the league is 4-4.
Third in points, three straight losses. Better than its record, and getting tired of hearing it.
Lost a game its bench could have won twice. Holding the last playoff spot by 53.02 points.
Six straight is over. Still 2-6. The bench, as ever, is in form.
One healthy quarterback in a two-quarterback league. Playoff odds 2%.

smart_move.stat_label: Lemon and Cooper, added Sunday afternoon
smart_move.headline: The team that never moves finally moved
smart_move.dek: AB81 made no transactions in seven weeks, then made three in three minutes on Sunday. It won by 1.58.
body: This beat has spent the season writing the same joke: AB81 doesn’t make moves. Zero of them through seven weeks. Then, at 3:06 p.m. Sunday, with the team deep in a hole against the champ, it dropped Mark Andrews and added Makai Lemon. At 3:08 Isiah Pacheco went. At 3:09 Darius Cooper arrived.

Both new players went straight into the lineup. Lemon scored 11.7. Cooper scored 3.9. That’s 15.6 points from players who weren’t on the roster at lunch. Andrews, the best option left on the bench, had scored 4.4.

AB81 won by 1.58. Take those moves away and the great Monday comeback falls short, and we’re writing about the champ’s miracle escape instead. Kirk Cousins scored more. Nothing mattered more. Seven weeks of silence, three minutes of work, one first-place team.

dumb_move.stat_label: Lamar Jackson, the week Rodgers was cut
dumb_move.headline: Cut the backup, lost the quarterback
dumb_move.dek: Santa Clara’s Finest released a quarterback for the second straight week. Then Lamar Jackson scored 0.0.
body: Last week’s Dumb Move: Santa Clara’s Finest cut Kirk Cousins mid-game on a Thursday. This week’s Dumb Move: at 5:46 p.m. Thursday, Santa Clara’s Finest cut Aaron Rodgers, in a two-quarterback league, to add Blake Corum. Repeat offenders are a proud tradition of this column.

Corum scored 13.3, so the transaction itself had a pulse. The problem is what it left: Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow, with nothing behind them. Jackson scored 0.0. Rodgers scored 5.88 for nobody, which isn’t much, but it’s infinitely more than zero. And 39 minutes after the Rodgers drop, Bad things man bad things picked up the very quarterback this team cut last week. Cousins scored 28.18.

The game was lost by 45.0, so this one didn’t change the result. It changes next week. The projected lineup has an empty QB slot, and the team is 1-7. Two straight weeks, two quarterbacks gone, one available quarterback left.

bench_beat.stat_label: Points on the bench in a 1.58-point loss
bench_beat.headline: Two different swaps would have won it
bench_beat.dek: Maye I touch your TDs? lost by 1.58. Its bench held two separate answers.
body: Bench Beat exists for weeks like this one, and last week’s winner of this award would like a word with this week’s. Maye I touch your TDs? lost 124.3 to 122.72 after leading by 79.62.

Exhibit A: Jaylen Waddle scored 14.9 on the bench while Drake London scored 1.8 in the lineup. That swap is worth 13.1. Exhibit B: Aaron Jones Sr. scored 6.0 on the bench while Zay Flowers scored 0.0 in the lineup. That one is worth 6.0. The margin was 1.58. Either swap alone wins this game.

Best possible lineup: 141.82. Actual: 122.72. A week after the bench was the difference for somebody else, it was the difference for the defending champ, and this one drops it to 2-6 with six games left.

swing_plays.headline: Forty-three yards, seventeen points
swing_plays.blurb: AB81 came in needing 40.75 from two players. One throw gave it 17.02 of them, and suddenly the champ’s 122.72 didn’t look like enough.

swing_plays.headline: The last lead change of the morning
swing_plays.blurb: Seven lead changes in 50 minutes, and this little 5-yard catch by Brock Bowers was the final one. Cherry Blossom never trailed again.

swing_plays.headline: One yard, and a tiebreak stays alive
swing_plays.blurb: Poochinski’s game was over. Its tiebreak wasn’t. Burden’s touchdown was 11.14 of the 34.91 it needed, and it finished 0.68 ahead of Bad things man bad things on points.

swing_plays.headline: Maye’s 48-yard strike
swing_plays.blurb: It looked like the dagger at the time: the champ’s lead went to 72.66. It wasn’t the dagger.

swing_plays.headline: Allen goes 21 yards, and the streak dies
swing_plays.blurb: Big Stric Energy’s lead was already huge. This run made it official, and Santa Clara’s Finest never got within shouting distance.

features.stat_label: Poochinski’s edge on points for second place
features.headline: One game settled three separate races
features.dek: AB81 got first place, Poochinski got second and deeboliciouskins got fourth, and all three came down to Monday numbers set that morning.
body: Monday morning’s brief said one game would decide first place, fourth place and the champ’s season. All three came through.

AB81 needed 40.75 and got 42.32: alone in first at 7-1. Poochinski’s trio needed 34.91 to pass Bad things man bad things on points and scored 35.58, so Bad things man bad things, finished at 181.84 and watching from home, slipped to third at 6-2 by 0.68 points. deeboliciouskins needed 23.87 from D’Andre Swift and Jason Myers to stay ahead of Cherry Blossom and got 28.9.
Add the champ, which fell to 2-6 with nobody left to play, and that’s four standings stories out of a single game. Only in this league.

features.headline: The week’s best back belonged to nobody
features.dek: Tyler Allgeier scored 36.1 without an owner. He out-scored every running back on every R.A.T.S. roster.
body: Bhayshul Tuten’s 29.9 was the best running-back game anyone actually started. Tyler Allgeier scored 36.1 on the waiver wire, where he remains as of this writing.

He had company. Adonai Mitchell scored 27.2 unrostered, Cam Ward 26.26 and Emmett Johnson 25.3. In a two-quarterback league, a free-agent quarterback scoring 26.26 should set off alarms. Jacoby Brissett started for the champ and scored 4.46.

The busiest team on the wire stayed busy: Bad things man bad things added Kirk Cousins, who scored 28.18. Isaiah Likely, dropped by that same team on Sunday morning, is now one of the better tight ends available, projected for 13.37.

features.headline: Three weeks left to make a trade
features.dek: Twenty-six weeks of history and not one deal. Santa Clara’s Finest has one healthy quarterback and a week to solve it.
body: The Week 11 deadline is three weeks away and the log still reads zero. Some of the math has changed. AB81 made its first moves of the season. The trade market has not.

The fit has never been cleaner. Bad things man bad things has four quarterbacks available and Cherry Blossom has four. Santa Clara’s Finest has one for two slots. Six teams make the playoffs, and Big Stric Energy, at 29.1%, is close enough to want help.
That’s what we said last week, too. The wire will do what it always does.

w9-m1.headline: Big Stric Energy gets a real test
w9-m1.blurb: Bad things man bad things projects for 163.88 to Big Stric Energy’s 152.91, a 60.4% edge. With a 53.02-point tiebreak gap to the champ, Big Stric Energy needs the win and the points. Metcalf’s bye is covered by Rashee Rice, if the front office lets him off the bench.

w9-m3.headline: The champ gets Poochinski next
w9-m3.blurb: Poochinski projects for 184.24, the best in the league, and is a 69.3% favorite. The champ has Brock Purdy back and projects for 163.13. It may also want a word with its own start/sit calls.

w9-m4.headline: First place visits the hottest team
w9-m4.blurb: AB81 is 7-1 and a 30.9% underdog. Cherry Blossom projects for 172.17 to 151.35, and the model has seen enough of this movie to say so. AB81 has made a career of ignoring it.

w9-m2.headline: The biggest spread on the board
w9-m2.blurb: deeboliciouskins is a 76.1% favorite, 159.34 to 129.79, even without Tony Pollard. Santa Clara’s Finest projects with an empty QB slot, and the wire will have to fill it before anything else matters.

playoff_note: Six weeks left, six playoff spots. AB81, Poochinski and Bad things man bad things are locked in the simulations, with Cherry Blossom (99.5%) and deeboliciouskins (99.1%) right behind them, and the top-two seed is the race among the top three: Poochinski 75.5%, Bad things man bad things 59%, AB81 44.7%. The last spot is the fight: Maye I touch your TDs? fell from 77.7% to 70.3%, Big Stric Energy climbed from 17.3% to 29.1%, and Santa Clara’s Finest is down to 2%.

waiver_targets.blurb: The top quarterback on the wire at a 17.48 projection. Santa Clara’s Finest has an empty QB slot and should claim him first.
Projected for 16.65, barely behind Willis. If Willis goes first, Santa Clara’s Finest takes this one.
Projected for 15.43 and available in a 2-QB league. The third answer to the same question.
Dropped by Bad things man bad things on Sunday. Projected for 13.37 on an 89% snap share. Anyone looking for a flex with a real role should look here.
Projected for 12.0, and AB81 has a WR slot projected at 5.02. That’s an easy claim.

usage_watch.blurb: Opportunities up from 10.4 to 24.0 a game on an 82% snap share. Scored 6.9 on the Bad things man bad things bench, but start him: the workload is real.
From 14.5 to 23.5 opportunities a game on an 80% snap share. Big Stric Energy has its running back. Keep starting him.
From 19.3 to 28.0 opportunities, but 40% of his points come from touchdowns. Start him and don’t pay extra for last week’s 27.9.
Opportunities down from 23.0 to 8.0 a game, snap share from 73% to 33%. His 6.0 would have won the champ a game, but don’t chase it. Bench him going forward.
From 22.3 to 11.0 opportunities a game. Still a name on the marquee, but Big Stric Energy should treat him as a flex, not a foundation.
Opportunities down from 23.3 to 16.0, and 40% of his points come from touchdowns. AB81 shouldn’t count on him as a weekly anchor.
